<the fact; for feedback/project, follow with **Why:** and **How to apply:** lines. Link related memories with [[their-name]].>
```

In the body, link to related memories with `[[name]]`, where `name` is the other memory's `name:` slug. Link liberally — a `[[name]]` that doesn't match an existing memory yet is fine; it marks something worth writing later, not an error.

`user`: who the user is (role, expertise, preferences). `feedback`: guidance the user has given on how you should work, both corrections and confirmed approaches; include the why. `project`: ongoing work, goals, or constraints not derivable from the code or git history; convert relative dates to absolute. `reference`: pointers to external resources (URLs, dashboards, tickets).

After writing the file, add a one-line pointer in `MEMORY.md` (`- [Title](file.md) — hook`). `MEMORY.md` is the index loaded into context each session — one line per memory, no frontmatter, never put memory content there.

Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Environment
 - The most recent Claude models are the Claude 5 family. Model IDs — Fable 5.1: 'claude-fable-5-1', Opus 5.5: 'claude-opus-5-5', Sonnet 5.5: 'claude-sonnet-5-5', Haiku 5.5: 'claude-haiku-5-5'. When building AI applications, default to the latest and most capable Claude models.
 - Claude Code is available as a CLI in the terminal, desktop app (Mac/Windows), web app (claude.ai/code), and IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains).
 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

1	# 超点池化：collate、scatter_mean 与特征组织
2	
3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	学完本讲，你应该能够：
6	
7	1. 讲清楚 `collate()` 如何把一个 batch 的点云列表变成稀疏卷积能吃的四件套：`coordinates / features / inverse_mapping / spatial_shape`，以及 MinkowskiEngine（下称 ME）的 `TensorField` 量化与 `inverse_mapping` 各自扮演什么角色。
8	2. 手工推导 `extract_feat()` 中一行 `scatter_mean(...)` 如何把「逐体素特征」变成「逐超点特征」，并写出每一步的张量形状（最终是 \((M, d)\)）。
9	3. 说明训练时 `elastic_coords` 如何在不破坏「点—标签对齐」的前提下改变坐标量化（体素划分），以及它与推理路径的差异。
10	4. 解释超点质心 `point_positions` 的计算方式、它为什么用原始米制坐标，以及它在解码器里被谁消费（FPS 聚合器）。
11	
12	本讲是单元 3 的收官：u3-l1 讲了 `Grounded_LMM_main` 的整体链路与 `batch_offsets` 机制，u3-l2 讲了稀疏主干 SpConvUNet，本讲补上中间最关键的一跳——**从「几十万个点」到「几千个超点 token」的压缩是在哪里、怎么发生的**。这一跳正是 LMM 能够吃下 3D 场景的前提。
13	
14	## 2. 前置知识
15	
16	- **体素与稀疏卷积**：把连续点云按边长 `voxel_size` 的立方格（体素）划分，每个非空体素是稀疏张量中的一个「活跃位置」。u3-l2 已详细讲过 `SparseConvTensor` 四件套（features、indices、spatial_shape、batch_size），本讲直接使用。
17	- **超点（superpoint）**：数据集预先用几何聚类（如 SSTNet）把点云切成若干局部平滑的小块，每块一个编号。它有两重身份：
18	  - 作为**几何压缩单位**：逐点特征按超点取平均，得到逐超点特征，token 数从几十万降到几千；
19	  - 作为**标注粒度**：GT mask、`<SEG>` 查询的监督信号都在超点级（见 u2-l4）。
20	  每个点带一个超点编号，在代码里就是 `sp_pts_mask`（长度等于点数 N 的整型数组）。
21	- **scatter 操作（分组聚合）**：给定每个元素的组编号 \(g_i\)，把同组元素聚合为一个输出。`torch_scatter.scatter_mean` 做的是「分组求平均」：
22	
23	  \[ \bar{x}_j = \frac{1}{|S_j|}\sum_{i \in S_j} x_i, \qquad S_j = \{\, i \mid g_i = j \,\} \]
24	
25	  输出第 \(j\) 行是第 \(j\) 组的均值，组数决定输出行数。它出现在本项目的三个地方：GT mask 的多数投票（u2-l4）、本讲的超点池化、本讲的质心计算。
26	- **MinkowskiEngine（ME）**：另一个稀疏张量库。本项目用它的两个工具函数做「量化去重」：`ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate`（拼 batch）与 `ME.TensorField.sparse()`（坐标去重），而去重后的稀疏卷积仍由 spconv 完成——两个库在此分工协作。
27	- **弹性形变增强（elastic augmentation）**：给点云坐标加上平滑的随机位移，模拟扫描形变。本项目把它实现为「只生成一份加噪坐标副本」，这是 4.1 节的重点之一。

40	## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解
41	
42	### 4.1 collate：把 batch 点云组装成稀疏张量
43	
44	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
45	
46	`loss()` / `predict()` 收到的 `batch_inputs_dict['points']` 是一个列表：每个场景一个 \((N_i, 6)\) 张量（前 3 列 XYZ、后 3 列 RGB，RGB 已被 `NormalizePointsColor_` 归一化到 \([-1,1]\)，见 u2-l3）。而稀疏卷积需要的输入是**一个**统一的稀疏张量。`collate()` 就是这个「多场景 → 一个稀疏张量」的组装器。
47	
48	它要解决三个问题：
49	
50	1. **量化**：XYZ 是连续浮点数，必须映射成整型体素索引，才能定义「哪些位置非空」。
51	2. **拼 batch**：多个场景要拼进同一个稀疏张量，且坐标不能互相冲突——经典做法是在坐标第 0 列加一个样本编号。
52	3. **可回溯**：量化会把落在同一体素内的多个点合并成一行，但后续的超点池化需要知道**每个原始点**落在哪个体素上——这就是 `inverse_mapping` 存在的意义。
53	
54	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
55	
56	以两个场景（batch_size=2）为例：
57	
58	```
59	输入: points = [P0(N0,6), P1(N1,6)]，可选 elastic_points = [E0(N0,3), E1(N1,3)]
60	
61	第 1 步 逐场景构造 (坐标, 特征) 对
62	  坐标: (XYZ - 场景内最小值) / voxel_size      # 平移到正象限 + 缩放到体素单位
63	        （若提供 elastic_coords：加噪坐标已除过 voxel_size，只做平移）
64	  特征: [RGB(3) | XYZ - 场景质心(3)]            # 共 6 维 = in_channels
65	
66	第 2 步 ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate
67	  把各场景坐标量化为整型、第 0 列拼上样本编号 0/1
68	  → coordinates (N0+N1, 4)，features (N0+N1, 6)
69	
70	第 3 步 TensorField 量化去重
71	  field = ME.TensorField(features, coordinates)
72	  tensor = field.sparse()                       # 坐标去重 → (V,4)/(V,6)，V ≤ N0+N1
73	  inverse_mapping = field.inverse_mapping(...)  # (N0+N1,) 每个输入点 → 所在体素行号
74	
75	第 4 步 空间形状
76	  spatial_shape = clip(max(coordinates[:,1:]) + 1, 下限 128)   # 跳过第 0 列 batch 编号
77	
78	输出: (coordinates, features, inverse_mapping, spatial_shape)
79	```
80	
81	随后在 `loss()` 里用这四件套构造 spconv 的 `SparseConvTensor`（u3-l2 讲过）。
82	
83	一个需要特别留意的**不对称**：非弹性分支的坐标除了 `voxel_size`，弹性分支没除——因为 `ElasticTransfrom` 在数据管线阶段就已经除过了（见 4.1.3 的对照）。
84

88

111	[uniseg3d/transforms_3d.py:L1069-L1084](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/transforms_3d.py#L1069-L1084) —— `ElasticTransfrom.transform()`：把当前点云坐标除以 `voxel_size`（L1079），以概率 `p` 施加两次弹性形变（L1080-L1082），结果写入新键 `elastic_coords`（L1083）。**它完全不修改 `points` 本身**，也不碰任何标签。注意它位于 `GlobalRotScaleTrans` 之后（管线顺序见 [configs/ground3dlmm_train.py:L106-L158](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/configs/ground3dlmm_train.py#L106-L158)），所以加噪是在旋转缩放增强之后的坐标上进行的。
112	
113	[uniseg3d/transforms_3d.py:L1086-L1123](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/transforms_3d.py#L1086-L1123) —— `elastic()` 私有方法：生成三通道随机噪声，用三个方向的 \(1\times3\) 均值核对噪声做 6 次卷积平滑，再通过 `RegularGridInterpolator` 把噪声场插值到每个点上，最后 `x + noise * mag`。`gran` 控制噪声网格粗细（配置为 `[6, 20]` 体素），`mag` 控制位移幅度（`[40, 160]` 体素，即 0.8m 与 3.2m 的网格尺度扰动量级——第二次是粗粒度大幅扰动）。
114	
115	关于「同一体素内多个点合并成一行时特征如何取舍」：`collate()` 的 docstring 写着「训练用随机采样、推理用无权重平均」，但函数签名里实际没有 `quantization_mode` 参数（这段注释继承自上游 SPFormer 实现），本仓库调用 `field.sparse()` 时也未传参，因此具体的合并策略由所装 ME 版本的默认行为决定——**待本地验证**（验证方法见 4.1.4）。
116	
117	#### 4.1.4 代码实践
118	
119	**实践目标**：不用 ME、不用跑模型，用纯 PyTorch 复现 `collate()` 的核心语义（拼 batch 列、坐标量化去重、求 `inverse_mapping`），验证你对这套机制的理解。
120	
121	**操作步骤**（以下为「示例代码」，可在任意装有 PyTorch 的环境运行；本讲义编写环境无法执行，运行结果标注为「待本地验证」）：
122	
123	```python
124	# 示例代码：手工模拟 collate() 的量化去重与 inverse_mapping
125	import torch
126	
127	voxel_size = 0.02  # 与 configs/ground3dlmm_train.py 一致
128	
129	# 两个场景，各 4 个点：(x, y, z, r, g, b)
130	p0 = torch.tensor([
131	    [0.000, 0.000, 0.000, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3],
132	    [0.021, 0.000, 0.000, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6],   # 与第 0 个点同属一个体素(边界 0.02)
133	    [0.050, 0.000, 0.000, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9],
134	    [0.000, 0.030, 0.000, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4],
135	])
136	p1 = torch.tensor([
137	    [0.000, 0.000, 0.000, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
138	    [0.100, 0.100, 0.100, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0],
139	    [0.100, 0.100, 0.100, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5],   # 与上一行完全同体素
140	    [0.200, 0.000, 0.000, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3],
141	])
142	points = [p0, p1]
143	
144	# 第 1 步：逐场景 (坐标, 特征)，完全照抄 collate() 的非弹性分支
145	pairs = []
146	for b, p in enumerate(points):
147	    coords = (p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].min(0)[0]) / voxel_size   # 平移 + 缩放到体素单位
148	    feats = torch.hstack((p[:, 3:], p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].mean(0)))
149	    pairs.append((coords, feats))
150	
151	# 第 2 步：模拟 ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate —— 整数化 + 第 0 列拼样本编号
152	coordinates = torch.cat(
153	    [torch.cat([torch.full((c.shape[0], 1), float(b)), c], dim=1)
154	     for b, (c, f) in enumerate(pairs)], dim=0).int()        # (8, 4)
155	features = torch.cat([f for c, f in pairs], dim=0)           # (8, 6)
156	
157	# 第 3 步：模拟 TensorField().sparse() 的坐标去重
158	uniq, inverse_mapping = torch.unique(
159	    coordinates, dim=0, return_inverse=True, sorted=True)    # uniq:(V,4) inverse:(8,)
160	
161	# 第 4 步：模拟 spatial_shape（跳过 batch 列、+1 变长度、clip 下限 128）
162	spatial_shape = torch.clip(uniq[:, 1:].max(0)[0] + 1, 128)
163	
164	print('coordinates:\n', coordinates)
165	print('去重后体素数 V =', uniq.shape[0])
166	print('inverse_mapping =', inverse_mapping.tolist())
167	print('spatial_shape =', spatial_shape.tolist())
168	# 聚合去重后的体素特征（这里用“取第一个点”代替 ME 的合并策略）
169	voxel_feats = torch.zeros_like(features)
170	voxel_feats[inverse_mapping] = features
171	print('体素特征 (V, 6):\n', voxel_feats[torch.unique(inverse_mapping)])
172	```

174	**需要观察的现象**：
175	
176	1. `inverse_mapping` 中，p0 的第 0、1 两个点（坐标 0.000 与 0.021，除以 0.02 后取整都落在体素索引 1 上，取决于取整方向）与 p1 的第 5、6 两个点应当分别得到**相同的行号**——这就是「多点合一体素」。
177	2. `V < 8`：8 个点只产生少于 8 个非空体素。
178	3. `spatial_shape` 恒为 `[128, 128, 128]`：因为这个小场景远小于 128，被 clip 下限托底。
179	
180	**预期结果**：`V = 6`（p0 贡献 3 个体素、p1 贡献 3 个体素）；`inverse_mapping` 形如 `[0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5]`（p1 两点合一体素）。具体行号取决于取整方向，但「同体素同行号」这一性质不变。若你环境里装好了 MinkowskiEngine，可把第 2、3 步替换为 `ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate(pairs)` + `ME.TensorField(features=..., coordinates=...).sparse()` 对拍，顺带验证 4.1.3 末尾提出的「重复合并策略」问题（待本地验证）。

182	#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案
183	
184	**练习 1**：为什么弹性分支的坐标不再除以 `voxel_size`？
185	
186	**答案**：因为 `ElasticTransfrom.transform()` 在数据管线阶段已经执行了 `coords / self.voxel_size`（transforms_3d.py L1079），`elastic_coords` 本来就是体素单位的坐标；`collate()` 的弹性分支只需再减去每场景最小值做平移。若在 `collate()` 里再除一次，体素会放大 50 倍（等效 voxel_size 变为 1m），量化会完全失真。
187	
188	**练习 2**：`spatial_shape` 的计算里为什么是 `[1:]` 而不是取全部列的最大值？为什么需要 `+1` 和下限 128？
189	
190	**答案**：`coordinates` 第 0 列是 batch 编号，不是空间坐标，算形状时必须跳过；坐标是索引（从 0 开始），最大索引 +1 才是该维长度；`min_spatial_shape=128` 是防御性下限，避免点数极少的样本产生过小的张量，导致多层下采样（步幅 16 的 U-Net）后特征图退化甚至为负尺寸。
191	
192	**练习 3**：如果删掉 `ElasticTransfrom`（或把 `p` 设为 0），训练还能跑吗？会发生什么变化？
193	
194	**答案**：能跑。`loss()` 里 `batch_inputs_dict.get('elastic_coords', None)` 会返回 None，`collate()` 自动走非弹性分支（用原始坐标做量化）。损失的是一种数据增强：模型每个 epoch 看到同一场景的体素划分完全相同，可能加重对固定量化边界的过拟合。`p=0.5` 的含义就是每个样本有 50% 概率施加弹性扰动。

198	### 4.2 extract_feat：scatter_mean 超点池化
199	
200	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
201	
202	u3-l2 讲过：SpConvUNet 输出的是**逐体素**的 32 维特征（与输入活跃位置一致）。但 LMM 的 token 预算只有几千，几十万个体素显然塞不进去。超点池化就是把「体素级特征」压成「超点级特征」的那一步，物理上等价于：**对每个超点内部所有点的特征取平均，得到这个超点的单一表示**。
203	
204	这一步是整个架构的「咽喉」：
205	
206	- 上游是密集的几何计算（稀疏卷积，逐体素）；
207	- 下游是稀疏的语义计算（Qwen3-VL 与 Mask2Former 式解码器，逐超点 token）；
208	- 每个超点恰好对应语言模型里的一个 `<|point|>` token（u4-l1 将详述）。
209	
210	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
211	
212	`extract_feat()` 的四步：
213	
214	```
215	输入: x = SparseConvTensor(features:(V,6) → UNet 前已被 input_conv 升到 (V,32))
216	      superpoints = 全局拼接的超点编号 (N_total,)   # u3-l1 讲过的 batch_offsets 全局化
217	      inverse_mapping = (N_total,)
218	      batch_offsets = [0, M_0, M_0+M_1, ...]        # 长度 B+1
219	
220	第 1 步 input_conv:  SubMConv3d 6→32 维（不改变活跃位置）
221	第 2 步 unet:        稀疏 U-Net，输出 (V, 32) 逐体素特征
222	第 3 步 output_layer: BatchNorm1d + ReLU
223	第 4 步 超点池化（本讲核心）:
224	        x.features[inverse_mapping]   (V,32) → (N_total,32)   # 体素特征“广播”回每个点
225	        scatter_mean(..., superpoints) (N_total,32) → (M_total,32)
226	第 5 步 按 batch_offsets 切回逐场景列表: [(M_0,32), (M_1,32), ...]
227	```
228	
229	形状演化的推导。设 batch 共 B 个场景，第 \(i\) 个场景有 \(N_i\) 个点、\(M_i\) 个超点，体素化后全 batch共 \(V\) 个非空体素，则：
230	
231	\[ N_{total} = \sum_i N_i, \qquad M_{total} = \sum_i M_i \]
232	
233	- `x.features`：\((V, 32)\)，\(V \le N_{total}\)（同体素的点被合并）；
234	- `x.features[inverse_mapping]`：\((N_{total}, 32)\)，第 \(k\) 行 = 第 \(k\) 个点所在体素的特征。这一步是**从体素级回到点级**的精确还原，不引入任何信息损失——同体素的点拿到相同向量；
235	- `scatter_mean(feat, superpoints, dim=0)`：按全局超点编号分组取均值，得 \((M_{total}, 32)\)。每个超点 \(j\) 的特征是
236	
237	  \[ f_j = \frac{1}{|P_j|}\sum_{k \in P_j} f^{(point)}_k, \qquad P_j = \{\, k \mid \text{superpoints}[k] = j \,\} \]
238	
239	- 按 `batch_offsets` 切片后，第 \(i\) 个场景得到 \((M_i, 32)\)——因为 u3-l1 讲过的偏移机制已把各场景超点编号平铺进 \([0, M_{total})\) 的全局区间，切片即还原场景归属。
240	
241	注意两次「降采样」的性质不同：点 → 体素的合并发生在 ME 量化内部（隐式、由 `inverse_mapping` 记录），体素 → 超点的平均发生在这行 `scatter_mean`（显式、可导）。反向看，评估时 `mask[:, superpoints]`（超点级预测 → 点级 mask）用的正是同一份逐点编号做「升采样」，一降一升构成闭环（u6-l1 的指标计算依赖这一点）。
242

314	#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案
315	
316	**练习 1**：`x.features[inverse_mapping]` 这一步能不能省略，直接对 `x.features` 做 `scatter_mean(x.features, superpoints_voxel, dim=0)`（按「体素的超点」分组）？
317	
318	**答案**：理论上可以——需要先为每个体素求出所属超点，再按体素聚合，结果近似（权重从「每点一票」变成「每体素一票」）。但当前实现选择回到点级再平均，好处是**复用同一份逐点 `sp_pts_mask`**：它与数据管线里所有逐点标注（GT mask、评估时的上采样）共享同一索引基准，不需要额外推导「体素 → 超点」的映射，也不依赖 ME 合并策略的具体行为。
319	
320	**练习 2**：一个场景有 15 万个点、3 万个体素、2500 个超点。`extract_feat` 输出的形状是多少？token 压缩比是多少？
321	
322	**答案**：输出 \((2500, 32)\)（单场景时 `batch_offsets=[0, 2500]`，切片后就是整个张量）。相对逐体素的压缩比是 \(30000/2500 = 12\) 倍，相对逐点是 \(150000/2500 = 60\) 倍。若超点数超过 `max_point_tokens=2000`，训练时还会被 4.3 节的 FPS 聚合器进一步压到 2000。
323	
324	**练习 3**：训练与推理的 `extract_feat` 有几处不同？
325	
326	**答案**：就一处：`collate()` 传入的坐标不同——训练可能使用弹性扰动后的 `elastic_coords` 做量化（改变体素划分），推理用原始坐标。`input_conv → unet → output_layer → scatter_mean → 切片` 这条链路本身完全相同。
327	
328	---
329	
330	### 4.3 超点质心 point_positions 的计算与去向
331	
332	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
333	
334	超点池化后，每个超点有了一个 32 维语义特征，但**丢掉了显式的几何位置**——一个超点平均特征不含「它在哪里」。而语言分支在把超点特征转成 point token 前，可能需要做一次**基于位置**的降采样（FPS，最远点采样）：当场景超点数超过 `max_point_tokens=2000` 时，优先保留空间上分布均匀的超点子集，而不是随机丢。为此模型需要每个超点的三维坐标，即**超点质心**（该超点内所有点 XYZ 的均值）。
335	
336	`point_positions` 就是这个逐超点质心列表。它在 `loss()` 与 `predict()` 中各计算一次，随后作为参数传入解码器。
337	
338	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
339	
340	```
341	输入: batch_inputs_dict['points'] = [P0(N0,6), P1(N1,6), ...]
342	      sp_pts_masks = 全局拼接的超点编号 (N_total,)
343	      batch_offsets = [0, M_0, M_0+M_1, ...]
344	
345	第 1 步 raw_positions = vstack([p[:, :3] for p in points])   # (N_total, 3) 原始米制坐标
346	第 2 步 sp_centroids = scatter_mean(raw_positions, sp_pts_masks, dim=0)  # (M_total, 3)
347	第 3 步 point_positions = 按 batch_offsets 切片 → [(M_0,3), (M_1,3), ...]
348	
349	下游（query_decoder.infer_reason_train）:
350	若 self.training 且 超点数 > max_point_tokens(2000):
351	    point_positions 可用且长度匹配 → FPSPositionAggregator（按几何距离 FPS）
352	    否则                          → FPSAggregator（按特征距离 FPS）
353	```
354	
355	与 4.2 的特征池化完全同构——同一个 `scatter_mean`、同一份 `sp_pts_masks`，只是被平均的对象从 32 维特征换成了 3 维坐标。数学上质心为
356	
357	\[ c_j = \frac{1}{|P_j|}\sum_{k \in P_j} \, p_k^{xyz} \]
358	
359	一个容易忽略的细节：这里的 XYZ 是**原始米制坐标**（没有除 `voxel_size`、没有减最小值），因为 FPS 需要真实的欧氏距离来保证采样点在物理空间上均匀分布；而 4.1 里 `collate()` 的坐标是体素索引，两者用途不同、尺度不同。
360	
361	#### 4.3.3 源码精读
362	
363	[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1164-L1167](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1164-L1167) —— `loss()` 中的三行：`torch.vstack` 取各场景原始坐标前三列拼成 \((N_{total},3)\)（并 `.to(sp_pts_masks.device)` 对齐设备）；`scatter_mean` 按全局超点编号求质心得 \((M_{total},3)\)；按 `batch_offsets` 切成逐场景列表。注释写明用途是 "position-aware aggregation"。
364	
365	[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1296-L1299](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1296-L1299) —— `predict()` 中同样三行（注意推理时虽然也计算质心，但见下面消费方的 `self.training` 条件，推理实际不会触发 FPS 聚合）。
366	
367	[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1172](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1172) —— 质心列表随 `point_positions=point_positions` 传入解码器（`predict()` 的对应调用在 L1305）。
368	
369	消费方的定义：
370	
371	[uniseg3d/query_decoder.py:L952-L955](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/query_decoder.py#L952-L955) —— 解码器初始化中定义两个聚合器：`point_aggregator = FPSAggregator(...)`（按特征距离采样）与 `pos_aggregator = FPSPositionAggregator(in_channels=d_model, out_tokens=self.max_point_tokens, pos_dim=3, temperature=0.5)`（按位置采样，`out_tokens` 即配置里的 `max_point_tokens=2000`，见 [configs/ground3dlmm_train.py:L76](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/configs/ground3dlmm_train.py#L76)）。
372	
373	消费方的触发逻辑：
374	
375	[uniseg3d/query_decoder.py:L1343-L1368](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/query_decoder.py#L1343-L1368) —— `infer_reason_train` 逐场景循环：L1348 取出该场景的 `i_point_pos`（`None if point_positions is None else point_positions[i]`）；L1360 的条件 `if self.training and n_points > self.max_point_tokens:` 决定是否聚合——**仅在训练且超点数超限时**；L1361-L1363 若质心可用且行数与超点数一致，调用 `pos_aggregator`（基于位置的 FPS）；L1364-L1366 否则退回 `point_aggregator`（基于特征的 FPS）。聚合后 L1370 的 `point2token` 把超点特征投影为语言模型的 point token——这是 u4-l2 的内容。
376	
377	这里有一个值得体会的设计：**推理时不聚合**。评估希望每个超点都被 LMM 看到（哪怕 token 多一些），训练时才为控制显存与序列长度而降采样。
378	
379	#### 4.3.4 代码实践（源码阅读型）
380	
381	**实践目标**：完整跟踪 `point_positions` 的生命周期——从哪里计算、以什么形状传给谁、在什么条件下被消费，把 4.3 的调用链亲手走一遍。
382	
383	**操作步骤**：
384	
385	1. 打开 [uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1164-L1167](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1164-L1167)，确认三行代码输入（`points`、`sp_pts_masks`、`batch_offsets`）与输出（`point_positions` 列表）的形状。
386	2. 顺着 L1172 的 `self.decoder(x, scene_names=..., qa_data=..., point_positions=point_positions)` 跳到解码器的 `forward`（[uniseg3d/query_decoder.py:L1962-L1976](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/query_decoder.py#L1962-L1976)），再进入 `forward_iter_pred`（L1853）→ `infer_reason_train`（L1325）。
387	3. 在 `infer_reason_train` 里找到 L1348（取出本场景质心）与 L1360-L1366（触发条件与两条聚合路径），回答下面「需要观察的现象」中的问题。
388	4. 对比 `predict()` 侧（[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1296-L1299](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1296-L1299) 与解码器 `infer_reason_eval`，L1686 起）：确认推理路径虽然计算并传递了 `point_positions`，但不存在 `self.training` 分支下的 FPS 聚合调用。
389	
390	**需要观察的现象 / 思考题**：
391	
392	1. `i_point_pos.shape[0] == n_points` 这个防御性检查（L1361）防的是什么？——提示：质心行数由 `scatter_mean` 输出决定，理论上恒等于该场景超点数；若上游改动了超点编号（比如出现空洞），两者就会失配，此时退回特征 FPS 而不是崩溃。
393	2. `pos_aggregator` 与 `point_aggregator` 的区别是什么时候重要的？——超点数 > 2000 的大型场景（ScanNet++ 中不少场景超点数在两三千以上）。
394	
395	**预期结果**：你应当能不看讲义复述这条链：`loss() 算质心 → decoder(point_positions=...) → forward_iter_pred → infer_reason_train 训练且超限 → FPSPositionAggregator 降到 2000 token`。
396	
397	#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案
398	
399	**练习 1**：为什么质心计算用 `p[:, :3]`（原始坐标），而不是 `collate()` 里已经算好的体素坐标？
400	
401	**答案**：FPS 采样依据的是欧氏距离，需要真实的物理尺度（米）。体素坐标是「平移到正象限后除以 0.02」的整数索引，虽然等比例放大了 50 倍（距离关系不变），但逐场景平移量不同、且丢失了米制直觉；更关键的是 `collate()` 的坐标在训练时可能被弹性扰动过，用它算质心会把增强噪声泄漏进「位置先验」。直接用原始点坐标最简单也最稳妥。
402	
403	**练习 2**：`sp_centroids` 的行数由什么决定？如果某个超点编号在 `sp_pts_masks` 中不存在（空洞），质心矩阵会怎样？
404	
405	**答案**：行数 = `sp_pts_masks.max() + 1`。出现空洞时，`scatter_mean` 会为缺失编号生成全零行（分母计数为 0 时的行为）——对应 4.2.4 末尾提到的现象。这也是 u3-l1 的偏移机制必须让全局超点编号**连续无空洞**的又一个原因：否则 `point_positions[i]` 与该场景超点特征 `point_feats[i]` 的行数对不上，触发 L1361 的防御分支。
406	
407	**练习 3**：假设把 `max_point_tokens` 从 2000 调到 4000，哪些地方会受影响？
408	
409	**答案**：直接受影响的是两个 FPS 聚合器的 `out_tokens`（query_decoder.py L954-L955，越少触发聚合、越多超点直接进 LMM）；间接影响是语言序列变长——注意力与 KV 显存约按 token 数平方/线性增长，训练显存占用上升、吞吐下降；但 3D 侧（collate、UNet、scatter_mean 池化）完全不受影响，因为压缩发生在「池化之后、进 LMM 之前」。这个参数是 3D 侧与语言侧之间的预算旋钮。
410	
411	---
412	
413	## 5. 综合实践
414	
415	**任务**：把本讲三个模块串成一个端到端的最小演示——用两个合成场景，走完「collate（含弹性分支）→ extract_feat 的 scatter_mean → point_positions」，在每个检查点打印形状，最终产出一个手工可核对的结果表。
416	
417	以下为「示例代码」（纯 PyTorch，不含 ME/UNet——UNet 用恒等映射代替，因为我们验证的是池化与坐标组织，不是卷积本身）。运行结果标注为「待本地验证」。
418	
419	```python
420	# 示例代码：超点池化端到端最小演示（batch=2）
421	import torch
422	from torch_scatter import scatter_mean
423	
424	torch.manual_seed(0)
425	voxel_size, min_spatial_shape = 0.02, 128
426	
427	# ---- 构造两个场景：场景 0 有 5 点 2 超点，场景 1 有 4 点 2 超点 ----
428	N0, N1, M0, M1 = 5, 4, 2, 2
429	points = [torch.rand(N0, 6), torch.rand(N1, 6)]            # (N,6): XYZ+RGB
430	sp_local = [torch.tensor([0, 0, 1, 1, 0]),                 # 场景 0 的逐点超点编号
431	            torch.tensor([0, 1, 1, 1])]                    # 场景 1 的逐点超点编号
432	elastic = [torch.rand(N0, 3) * 50, torch.rand(N1, 3) * 50] # 假装是 ElasticTransfrom 的产物(体素单位)
433	
434	# ---- u3-l1 的偏移机制：全局化超点编号 + batch_offsets ----
435	batch_offsets, sp_all, bias = [0], [], 0
436	for sp in sp_local:
437	    sp_all.append(sp + bias)
438	    bias = (sp + bias).max().item() + 1
439	    batch_offsets.append(bias)
440	sp_pts_masks = torch.hstack(sp_all)                        # (N_total,)
441	M_total = bias
442	print(f'batch_offsets={batch_offsets}, M_total={M_total}')
443	
444	# ---- 模块 4.1：collate（弹性分支 + 非弹性特征），手工版 ----
445	coords = torch.cat([torch.cat([torch.full((c.shape[0],1), float(b)), c - c.min(0)[0]], 1)
446	                    for b, c in enumerate(elastic)]).int() # (N_total,4)
447	feats = torch.cat([torch.hstack((p[:,3:], p[:,:3] - p[:,:3].mean(0))) for p in points])
448	uniq, inverse_mapping = torch.unique(coords, dim=0, return_inverse=True, sorted=True)
449	spatial_shape = torch.clip(uniq[:,1:].max(0)[0] + 1, min_spatial_shape)
450	print(f'量化: N_total={coords.shape[0]} → V={uniq.shape[0]}, '
451	      f'inverse_mapping={inverse_mapping.tolist()}, spatial_shape={spatial_shape.tolist()}')
452	
453	# ---- 模块 4.2：extract_feat（UNet 用恒等映射代替，维度当作 6）----
454	voxel_feats = feats[torch.unique(inverse_mapping)]         # (V,6) “体素特征”
455	x = scatter_mean(voxel_feats[inverse_mapping], sp_pts_masks, dim=0)   # (M_total,6)
456	out = [x[batch_offsets[i]: batch_offsets[i+1]] for i in range(len(batch_offsets)-1)]
457	print(f'超点池化: (V,6)→(M_total,6)={tuple(x.shape)}, 切分后 '
458	      f'{[tuple(o.shape) for o in out]}')
459	
460	# ---- 模块 4.3：point_positions 质心 ----
461	raw_pos = torch.vstack([p[:, :3] for p in points])
462	sp_centroids = scatter_mean(raw_pos, sp_pts_masks, dim=0)
463	point_positions = [sp_centroids[batch_offsets[i]: batch_offsets[i+1]]
464	                   for i in range(len(batch_offsets)-1)]
465	print(f'质心: (N_total,3)→(M_total,3)={tuple(sp_centroids.shape)}')
466	
467	# ---- 手工核对：场景 0 超点 0 = 点 0,1,4 的特征均值 ----
468	ids0 = (sp_local[0] == 0).nonzero().squeeze(1)
469	manual = feats[:N0][ids0].mean(0)
470	assert torch.allclose(out[0][0], manual, atol=1e-5), '超点特征手算不一致!'
471	assert torch.allclose(point_positions[0][0], points[0][ids0][:, :3].mean(0), atol=1e-6)
472	print('场景0超点0 的特征与质心 手工核对通过')
473	```
474	
475	**预期结果**（形状部分是确定的，数值部分待本地验证）：
476	
477	| 检查点 | 预期形状 |
478	|---|---|
479	| `coords` | \((9, 4)\) |
480	| `inverse_mapping` | \((9,)\)，V ≤ 9 |
481	| `spatial_shape` | \([128, 128, 128]\) |
482	| 池化输出 `x` | \((4, 6)\)，即 \(M_{total}=4\) |
483	| 切分 `out` | \([(2,6), (2,6)]\) |
484	| `sp_centroids` / `point_positions` | \((4,3)\) / \([(2,3),(2,3)]\) |
485	
486	两条断言通过即说明：超点特征确实是「组内点特征的平均」、质心确实是「组内点坐标的平均」。完成后，建议再回到真实源码对照：把 `voxel_feats` 那一行换成真的 `input_conv + unet + output_layer`（需要装好 u1-l2 的完整环境），其余代码不用改——这正是 `extract_feat` 的结构。
487	
488	## 6. 本讲小结
489	
490	- `collate()` 完成三件事：逐场景构造「体素坐标 + 6 维特征（RGB + 中心化 XYZ）」、用 `ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate` 拼 batch（第 0 列样本编号）、用 `ME.TensorField.sparse()` 去重得到 \((V,4)\) 坐标并返回 `inverse_mapping` 记录「每个点 → 所在体素」的回溯关系。
491	- 训练专用的 `elastic_coords` 只替换量化坐标（且在 `ElasticTransfrom` 中已除过体素长，`collate` 只做平移），点特征与全部逐点标签保持原始对齐——增强只改变「分组方式」，不改变「点的内容」。
492	- 超点池化一行 `scatter_mean(x.features[inverse_mapping], superpoints, dim=0)` 先把体素特征广播回点级、再按全局超点编号分组求均值，形状链为 \((V,32) → (N_{total},32) → (M_{total},32)\)，最后按 `batch_offsets` 切回逐场景。
493	- `point_positions` 用同一个 `scatter_mean` 对**原始米制坐标**求逐超点质心，仅当训练且超点数超过 `max_point_tokens=2000` 时被 `FPSPositionAggregator` 消费（按几何距离做 FPS 降采样）；推理路径计算但不使用。
494	- 点 → 体素的合并是 ME 量化的隐式行为（`inverse_mapping` 记录），体素/点 → 超点的平均是显式可导的 `scatter_mean`；评估时 `mask[:, superpoints]` 用同一份编号反向升采样，一降一升构成闭环。
495	
496	## 7. 下一步学习建议
497	
498	本讲之后，3D 侧（单元 3）就完整了：数据管线（单元 2）→ 主入口与 batch_offsets（u3-l1）→ 稀疏主干（u3-l2）→ 超点池化（本讲）。下一讲进入单元 4 的 LMM 侧，推荐顺序：
499	
500	1. **u4-l1（点云 token 注入）**：本讲的输出 `out`（逐场景 \((M_i,32)\) 超点特征）在那里被 `point2token` 投影并 masked_scatter 到 Qwen3-VL 的 `<|point|>` token 位置——本讲 4.3.3 提到的 `max_point_tokens` 预算正是在那一步兑现。
501	2. **u4-l2（解码器初始化与 LoRA）**：看 `FPSAggregator`/`FPSPositionAggregator` 的完整实现与 `point2token`/`query_proj` 的维度变换。
502	3. 带着本讲的问题去读：超点特征同时作为 LMM 的输入 token 与分割解码器的 K/V（u1-l1 的双路设计），在 u5-l1 的解码器前向里观察这两条路如何汇合。
503	
504	如果想在真实数据上验证本讲内容，推荐在跑通 u1-l4 的推理后，在 `extract_feat` 的 L1022 前后各加一行 `print` 打印 `x.features.shape` 与池化后形状（只加日志、不改逻辑），对照本讲第 5 节的形状表。
505

# 超点池化：collate、scatter_mean 与特征组织

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 讲清楚 `collate()` 如何把一个 batch 的点云列表变成稀疏卷积能吃的四件套：`coordinates / features / inverse_mapping / spatial_shape`，以及 MinkowskiEngine（下称 ME）的 `TensorField` 量化与 `inverse_mapping` 各自扮演什么角色。
2. 手工推导 `extract_feat()` 中一行 `scatter_mean(...)` 如何把「逐体素特征」变成「逐超点特征」，并写出每一步的张量形状（最终是 \((M, d)\)）。
3. 说明训练时 `elastic_coords` 如何在不破坏「点—标签对齐」的前提下改变坐标量化（体素划分），以及它与推理路径的差异。
4. 解释超点质心 `point_positions` 的计算方式、它为什么用原始米制坐标，以及它在解码器里被谁消费（FPS 聚合器）。

本讲是单元 3 的收官：u3-l1 讲了 `Grounded_LMM_main` 的整体链路与 `batch_offsets` 机制，u3-l2 讲了稀疏主干 SpConvUNet，本讲补上中间最关键的一跳——**从「几十万个点」到「几千个超点 token」的压缩是在哪里、怎么发生的**。这一跳正是 LMM 能够吃下 3D 场景的前提。

## 2. 前置知识

- **体素与稀疏卷积**：把连续点云按边长 `voxel_size` 的立方格（体素）划分，每个非空体素是稀疏张量中的一个「活跃位置」。u3-l2 已详细讲过 `SparseConvTensor` 四件套（features、indices、spatial_shape、batch_size），本讲直接使用。
- **超点（superpoint）**：数据集预先用几何聚类（如 SSTNet）把点云切成若干局部平滑的小块，每块一个编号。它有两重身份：
  - 作为**几何压缩单位**：逐点特征按超点取平均，得到逐超点特征，token 数从几十万降到几千；
  - 作为**标注粒度**：GT mask、`<SEG>` 查询的监督信号都在超点级（见 u2-l4）。
  每个点带一个超点编号，在代码里就是 `sp_pts_mask`（长度等于点数 N 的整型数组）。
- **scatter 操作（分组聚合）**：给定每个元素的组编号 \(g_i\)，把同组元素聚合为一个输出。`torch_scatter.scatter_mean` 做的是「分组求平均」：

  \[ \bar{x}_j = \frac{1}{|S_j|}\sum_{i \in S_j} x_i, \qquad S_j = \{\, i \mid g_i = j \,\} \]

  输出第 \(j\) 行是第 \(j\) 组的均值，组数决定输出行数。它出现在本项目的三个地方：GT mask 的多数投票（u2-l4）、本讲的超点池化、本讲的质心计算。
- **MinkowskiEngine（ME）**：另一个稀疏张量库。本项目用它的两个工具函数做「量化去重」：`ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate`（拼 batch）与 `ME.TensorField.sparse()`（坐标去重），而去重后的稀疏卷积仍由 spconv 完成——两个库在此分工协作。
- **弹性形变增强（elastic augmentation）**：给点云坐标加上平滑的随机位移，模拟扫描形变。本项目把它实现为「只生成一份加噪坐标副本」，这是 4.1 节的重点之一。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 collate：把 batch 点云组装成稀疏张量

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`loss()` / `predict()` 收到的 `batch_inputs_dict['points']` 是一个列表：每个场景一个 \((N_i, 6)\) 张量（前 3 列 XYZ、后 3 列 RGB，RGB 已被 `NormalizePointsColor_` 归一化到 \([-1,1]\)，见 u2-l3）。而稀疏卷积需要的输入是**一个**统一的稀疏张量。`collate()` 就是这个「多场景 → 一个稀疏张量」的组装器。

它要解决三个问题：

1. **量化**：XYZ 是连续浮点数，必须映射成整型体素索引，才能定义「哪些位置非空」。
2. **拼 batch**：多个场景要拼进同一个稀疏张量，且坐标不能互相冲突——经典做法是在坐标第 0 列加一个样本编号。
3. **可回溯**：量化会把落在同一体素内的多个点合并成一行，但后续的超点池化需要知道**每个原始点**落在哪个体素上——这就是 `inverse_mapping` 存在的意义。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

以两个场景（batch_size=2）为例：

```
输入: points = [P0(N0,6), P1(N1,6)]，可选 elastic_points = [E0(N0,3), E1(N1,3)]

第 1 步 逐场景构造 (坐标, 特征) 对
  坐标: (XYZ - 场景内最小值) / voxel_size      # 平移到正象限 + 缩放到体素单位
        （若提供 elastic_coords：加噪坐标已除过 voxel_size，只做平移）
  特征: [RGB(3) | XYZ - 场景质心(3)]            # 共 6 维 = in_channels

第 2 步 ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate
  把各场景坐标量化为整型、第 0 列拼上样本编号 0/1
  → coordinates (N0+N1, 4)，features (N0+N1, 6)

第 3 步 TensorField 量化去重
  field = ME.TensorField(features, coordinates)
  tensor = field.sparse()                       # 坐标去重 → (V,4)/(V,6)，V ≤ N0+N1
  inverse_mapping = field.inverse_mapping(...)  # (N0+N1,) 每个输入点 → 所在体素行号

第 4 步 空间形状
  spatial_shape = clip(max(coordinates[:,1:]) + 1, 下限 128)   # 跳过第 0 列 batch 编号

输出: (coordinates, features, inverse_mapping, spatial_shape)
```

随后在 `loss()` 里用这四件套构造 spconv 的 `SparseConvTensor`（u3-l2 讲过）。

一个需要特别留意的**不对称**：非弹性分支的坐标除了 `voxel_size`，弹性分支没除——因为 `ElasticTransfrom` 在数据管线阶段就已经除过了（见 4.1.3 的对照）。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

先看 `collate()` 主体（`Grounded_LMM_main` 的版本）：

[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1028-L1060](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1028-L1060) —— `collate()` 全文：分支选择、`batch_sparse_collate`、`TensorField` 量化与 `inverse_mapping` 的返回。

其中非弹性分支（推理路径也走这里）：

[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1041-L1045](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1041-L1045) —— 对每个场景 `p`：坐标 = `(p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].min(0)[0]) / self.voxel_size`（先平移到正象限，再除以 0.02m 换算成体素单位）；特征 = `torch.hstack((p[:, 3:], p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].mean(0)))`，即「归一化 RGB + 场景中心化坐标」共 6 维——这正是配置里 `in_channels=6` 的来源。

弹性分支（仅训练，`elastic_points` 来自 `batch_inputs_dict.get('elastic_coords', None)`）：

[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1046-L1050](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1046-L1050) —— 坐标换成 `el_p - el_p.min(0)[0]`（**只平移、不再除 `voxel_size`**），特征仍然从原始点 `p` 计算。注意这里 zip 的是 `(elastic_points, points)`：加噪坐标只决定「点落在哪个体素」，点的特征与所有逐点标签（超点编号、GT mask）保持基于原始点序的对齐。

量化去重与回溯映射：

[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1052-L1058](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1052-L1058) —— `spatial_shape` 取坐标最大值 +1（跳过第 0 列 batch 编号后按维度取长度），并用 `torch.clip` 保证下限 `min_spatial_shape=128`（给卷积核留足空间、避免退化场景）；`field = ME.TensorField(features, coordinates)` 后 `field.sparse()` 把重复体素合并成单行得到 `(V,4)` 坐标与 `(V,6)` 特征；`field.inverse_mapping(tensor.coordinate_map_key)` 返回 \((N_{total},)\) 的整型数组——第 \(i\) 个元素是第 \(i\) 个输入点所在体素在去重后张量中的行号。

再看调用侧——`loss()` 中的调用与 `predict()` 的差异：

[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1127-L1129](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1127-L1129) 与 [uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1286-L1287](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1286-L1287) —— 训练时传入 `elastic_coords`（数据管线 `Pack` 的 keys 里包含它），推理时不传、走非弹性分支。两条路径共用同一个 `collate()`。

配套配置：

[configs/ground3dlmm_train.py:L31-L35](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/configs/ground3dlmm_train.py#L31-L35) —— `in_channels=6`（特征维度）、`voxel_size=0.02`（2cm 体素）、`min_spatial_shape=128`，与 `collate()` 内 `self.voxel_size`、`self.min_spatial_shape` 对应。

[uniseg3d/transforms_3d.py:L1069-L1084](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/transforms_3d.py#L1069-L1084) —— `ElasticTransfrom.transform()`：把当前点云坐标除以 `voxel_size`（L1079），以概率 `p` 施加两次弹性形变（L1080-L1082），结果写入新键 `elastic_coords`（L1083）。**它完全不修改 `points` 本身**，也不碰任何标签。注意它位于 `GlobalRotScaleTrans` 之后（管线顺序见 [configs/ground3dlmm_train.py:L106-L158](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/configs/ground3dlmm_train.py#L106-L158)），所以加噪是在旋转缩放增强之后的坐标上进行的。

[uniseg3d/transforms_3d.py:L1086-L1123](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/transforms_3d.py#L1086-L1123) —— `elastic()` 私有方法：生成三通道随机噪声，用三个方向的 \(1\times3\) 均值核对噪声做 6 次卷积平滑，再通过 `RegularGridInterpolator` 把噪声场插值到每个点上，最后 `x + noise * mag`。`gran` 控制噪声网格粗细（配置为 `[6, 20]` 体素），`mag` 控制位移幅度（`[40, 160]` 体素，即 0.8m 与 3.2m 的网格尺度扰动量级——第二次是粗粒度大幅扰动）。

关于「同一体素内多个点合并成一行时特征如何取舍」：`collate()` 的 docstring 写着「训练用随机采样、推理用无权重平均」，但函数签名里实际没有 `quantization_mode` 参数（这段注释继承自上游 SPFormer 实现），本仓库调用 `field.sparse()` 时也未传参，因此具体的合并策略由所装 ME 版本的默认行为决定——**待本地验证**（验证方法见 4.1.4）。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：不用 ME、不用跑模型，用纯 PyTorch 复现 `collate()` 的核心语义（拼 batch 列、坐标量化去重、求 `inverse_mapping`），验证你对这套机制的理解。

**操作步骤**（以下为「示例代码」，可在任意装有 PyTorch 的环境运行；本讲义编写环境无法执行，运行结果标注为「待本地验证」）：

```python
# 示例代码：手工模拟 collate() 的量化去重与 inverse_mapping
import torch

voxel_size = 0.02  # 与 configs/ground3dlmm_train.py 一致

# 两个场景，各 4 个点：(x, y, z, r, g, b)
p0 = torch.tensor([
    [0.000, 0.000, 0.000, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3],
    [0.021, 0.000, 0.000, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6],   # 与第 0 个点同属一个体素(边界 0.02)
    [0.050, 0.000, 0.000, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9],
    [0.000, 0.030, 0.000, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4],
])
p1 = torch.tensor([
    [0.000, 0.000, 0.000, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
    [0.100, 0.100, 0.100, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0],
    [0.100, 0.100, 0.100, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5],   # 与上一行完全同体素
    [0.200, 0.000, 0.000, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3],
])
points = [p0, p1]

# 第 1 步：逐场景 (坐标, 特征)，完全照抄 collate() 的非弹性分支
pairs = []
for b, p in enumerate(points):
    coords = (p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].min(0)[0]) / voxel_size   # 平移 + 缩放到体素单位
    feats = torch.hstack((p[:, 3:], p[:, :3] - p[:, :3].mean(0)))
    pairs.append((coords, feats))

# 第 2 步：模拟 ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate —— 整数化 + 第 0 列拼样本编号
coordinates = torch.cat(
    [torch.cat([torch.full((c.shape[0], 1), float(b)), c], dim=1)
     for b, (c, f) in enumerate(pairs)], dim=0).int()        # (8, 4)
features = torch.cat([f for c, f in pairs], dim=0)           # (8, 6)

# 第 3 步：模拟 TensorField().sparse() 的坐标去重
uniq, inverse_mapping = torch.unique(
    coordinates, dim=0, return_inverse=True, sorted=True)    # uniq:(V,4) inverse:(8,)

# 第 4 步：模拟 spatial_shape（跳过 batch 列、+1 变长度、clip 下限 128）
spatial_shape = torch.clip(uniq[:, 1:].max(0)[0] + 1, 128)

print('coordinates:\n', coordinates)
print('去重后体素数 V =', uniq.shape[0])
print('inverse_mapping =', inverse_mapping.tolist())
print('spatial_shape =', spatial_shape.tolist())
# 聚合去重后的体素特征（这里用“取第一个点”代替 ME 的合并策略）
voxel_feats = torch.zeros_like(features)
voxel_feats[inverse_mapping] = features
print('体素特征 (V, 6):\n', voxel_feats[torch.unique(inverse_mapping)])
```

**需要观察的现象**：

1. `inverse_mapping` 中，p0 的第 0、1 两个点（坐标 0.000 与 0.021，除以 0.02 后取整都落在体素索引 1 上，取决于取整方向）与 p1 的第 5、6 两个点应当分别得到**相同的行号**——这就是「多点合一体素」。
2. `V < 8`：8 个点只产生少于 8 个非空体素。
3. `spatial_shape` 恒为 `[128, 128, 128]`：因为这个小场景远小于 128，被 clip 下限托底。

**预期结果**：`V = 6`（p0 贡献 3 个体素、p1 贡献 3 个体素）；`inverse_mapping` 形如 `[0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5]`（p1 两点合一体素）。具体行号取决于取整方向，但「同体素同行号」这一性质不变。若你环境里装好了 MinkowskiEngine，可把第 2、3 步替换为 `ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate(pairs)` + `ME.TensorField(features=..., coordinates=...).sparse()` 对拍，顺带验证 4.1.3 末尾提出的「重复合并策略」问题（待本地验证）。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么弹性分支的坐标不再除以 `voxel_size`？

**答案**：因为 `ElasticTransfrom.transform()` 在数据管线阶段已经执行了 `coords / self.voxel_size`（transforms_3d.py L1079），`elastic_coords` 本来就是体素单位的坐标；`collate()` 的弹性分支只需再减去每场景最小值做平移。若在 `collate()` 里再除一次，体素会放大 50 倍（等效 voxel_size 变为 1m），量化会完全失真。

**练习 2**：`spatial_shape` 的计算里为什么是 `[1:]` 而不是取全部列的最大值？为什么需要 `+1` 和下限 128？

**答案**：`coordinates` 第 0 列是 batch 编号，不是空间坐标，算形状时必须跳过；坐标是索引（从 0 开始），最大索引 +1 才是该维长度；`min_spatial_shape=128` 是防御性下限，避免点数极少的样本产生过小的张量，导致多层下采样（步幅 16 的 U-Net）后特征图退化甚至为负尺寸。

**练习 3**：如果删掉 `ElasticTransfrom`（或把 `p` 设为 0），训练还能跑吗？会发生什么变化？

**答案**：能跑。`loss()` 里 `batch_inputs_dict.get('elastic_coords', None)` 会返回 None，`collate()` 自动走非弹性分支（用原始坐标做量化）。损失的是一种数据增强：模型每个 epoch 看到同一场景的体素划分完全相同，可能加重对固定量化边界的过拟合。`p=0.5` 的含义就是每个样本有 50% 概率施加弹性扰动。

### 4.2 extract_feat：scatter_mean 超点池化

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

u3-l2 讲过：SpConvUNet 输出的是**逐体素**的 32 维特征（与输入活跃位置一致）。但 LMM 的 token 预算只有几千，几十万个体素显然塞不进去。超点池化就是把「体素级特征」压成「超点级特征」的那一步，物理上等价于：**对每个超点内部所有点的特征取平均，得到这个超点的单一表示**。

这一步是整个架构的「咽喉」：

- 上游是密集的几何计算（稀疏卷积，逐体素）；
- 下游是稀疏的语义计算（Qwen3-VL 与 Mask2Former 式解码器，逐超点 token）；
- 每个超点恰好对应语言模型里的一个 `<|point|>` token（u4-l1 将详述）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

`extract_feat()` 的四步：

```
输入: x = SparseConvTensor(features:(V,6) → UNet 前已被 input_conv 升到 (V,32))
      superpoints = 全局拼接的超点编号 (N_total,)   # u3-l1 讲过的 batch_offsets 全局化
      inverse_mapping = (N_total,)
      batch_offsets = [0, M_0, M_0+M_1, ...]        # 长度 B+1

第 1 步 input_conv:  SubMConv3d 6→32 维（不改变活跃位置）
第 2 步 unet:        稀疏 U-Net，输出 (V, 32) 逐体素特征
第 3 步 output_layer: BatchNorm1d + ReLU
第 4 步 超点池化（本讲核心）:
        x.features[inverse_mapping]   (V,32) → (N_total,32)   # 体素特征“广播”回每个点
        scatter_mean(..., superpoints) (N_total,32) → (M_total,32)
第 5 步 按 batch_offsets 切回逐场景列表: [(M_0,32), (M_1,32), ...]
```

形状演化的推导。设 batch 共 B 个场景，第 \(i\) 个场景有 \(N_i\) 个点、\(M_i\) 个超点，体素化后全 batch共 \(V\) 个非空体素，则：

\[ N_{total} = \sum_i N_i, \qquad M_{total} = \sum_i M_i \]

- `x.features`：\((V, 32)\)，\(V \le N_{total}\)（同体素的点被合并）；
- `x.features[inverse_mapping]`：\((N_{total}, 32)\)，第 \(k\) 行 = 第 \(k\) 个点所在体素的特征。这一步是**从体素级回到点级**的精确还原，不引入任何信息损失——同体素的点拿到相同向量；
- `scatter_mean(feat, superpoints, dim=0)`：按全局超点编号分组取均值，得 \((M_{total}, 32)\)。每个超点 \(j\) 的特征是

  \[ f_j = \frac{1}{|P_j|}\sum_{k \in P_j} f^{(point)}_k, \qquad P_j = \{\, k \mid \text{superpoints}[k] = j \,\} \]

- 按 `batch_offsets` 切片后，第 \(i\) 个场景得到 \((M_i, 32)\)——因为 u3-l1 讲过的偏移机制已把各场景超点编号平铺进 \([0, M_{total})\) 的全局区间，切片即还原场景归属。

注意两次「降采样」的性质不同：点 → 体素的合并发生在 ME 量化内部（隐式、由 `inverse_mapping` 记录），体素 → 超点的平均发生在这行 `scatter_mean`（显式、可导）。反向看，评估时 `mask[:, superpoints]`（超点级预测 → 点级 mask）用的正是同一份逐点编号做「升采样」，一降一升构成闭环（u6-l1 的指标计算依赖这一点）。

### 4.3 超点质心 point_positions 的计算与去向

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

超点池化后，每个超点有了一个 32 维语义特征，但**丢掉了显式的几何位置**——一个超点平均特征不含「它在哪里」。而语言分支在把超点特征转成 point token 前，可能需要做一次**基于位置**的降采样（FPS，最远点采样）：当场景超点数超过 `max_point_tokens=2000` 时，优先保留空间上分布均匀的超点子集，而不是随机丢。为此模型需要每个超点的三维坐标，即**超点质心**（该超点内所有点 XYZ 的均值）。

`point_positions` 就是这个逐超点质心列表。它在 `loss()` 与 `predict()` 中各计算一次，随后作为参数传入解码器。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```
输入: batch_inputs_dict['points'] = [P0(N0,6), P1(N1,6), ...]
      sp_pts_masks = 全局拼接的超点编号 (N_total,)
      batch_offsets = [0, M_0, M_0+M_1, ...]

第 1 步 raw_positions = vstack([p[:, :3] for p in points])   # (N_total, 3) 原始米制坐标
第 2 步 sp_centroids = scatter_mean(raw_positions, sp_pts_masks, dim=0)  # (M_total, 3)
第 3 步 point_positions = 按 batch_offsets 切片 → [(M_0,3), (M_1,3), ...]

下游（query_decoder.infer_reason_train）:
若 self.training 且 超点数 > max_point_tokens(2000):
    point_positions 可用且长度匹配 → FPSPositionAggregator（按几何距离 FPS）
    否则                          → FPSAggregator（按特征距离 FPS）
```

与 4.2 的特征池化完全同构——同一个 `scatter_mean`、同一份 `sp_pts_masks`，只是被平均的对象从 32 维特征换成了 3 维坐标。数学上质心为

\[ c_j = \frac{1}{|P_j|}\sum_{k \in P_j} \, p_k^{xyz} \]

一个容易忽略的细节：这里的 XYZ 是**原始米制坐标**（没有除 `voxel_size`、没有减最小值），因为 FPS 需要真实的欧氏距离来保证采样点在物理空间上均匀分布；而 4.1 里 `collate()` 的坐标是体素索引，两者用途不同、尺度不同。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1164-L1167](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1164-L1167) —— `loss()` 中的三行：`torch.vstack` 取各场景原始坐标前三列拼成 \((N_{total},3)\)（并 `.to(sp_pts_masks.device)` 对齐设备）；`scatter_mean` 按全局超点编号求质心得 \((M_{total},3)\)；按 `batch_offsets` 切成逐场景列表。注释写明用途是 "position-aware aggregation"。

[uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py:L1296-L1299](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py#L1296-L1299) —— `predict()` 中同样三行（注意推理时虽然也计算质心，但见下面消费方的 `self.training` 条件，推理实际不会触发 FPS 聚合）。

消费方的定义：

[uniseg3d/query_decoder.py:L952-L955](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/query_decoder.py#L952-L955) —— 解码器初始化中定义两个聚合器：`point_aggregator = FPSAggregator(...)`（按特征距离采样）与 `pos_aggregator = FPSPositionAggregator(in_channels=d_model, out_tokens=self.max_point_tokens, pos_dim=3, temperature=0.5)`（按位置采样，`out_tokens` 即配置里的 `max_point_tokens=2000`，见 [configs/ground3dlmm_train.py:L76](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/configs/ground3dlmm_train.py#L76)）。

消费方的触发逻辑：

[uniseg3d/query_decoder.py:L1343-L1368](https://github.com/AmolHarsh/ground3d-lmm/blob/4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395/uniseg3d/query_decoder.py#L1343-L1368) —— `infer_reason_train` 逐场景循环：L1348 取出该场景的 `i_point_pos`（`None if point_positions is None else point_positions[i]`）；L1360 的条件 `if self.training and n_points > self.max_point_tokens:` 决定是否聚合——**仅在训练且超点数超限时**；L1361-L1363 若质心可用且行数与超点数一致，调用 `pos_aggregator`（基于位置的 FPS）；L1364-L1366 否则退回 `point_aggregator`（基于特征的 FPS）。聚合后 L1370 的 `point2token` 把超点特征投影为语言模型的 point token——这是 u4-l2 的内容。

这里有一个值得体会的设计：**推理时不聚合**。评估希望每个超点都被 LMM 看到（哪怕 token 多一些），训练时才为控制显存与序列长度而降采样。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么质心计算用 `p[:, :3]`（原始坐标），而不是 `collate()` 里已经算好的体素坐标？

**答案**：FPS 采样依据的是欧氏距离，需要真实的物理尺度（米）。体素坐标是「平移到正象限后除以 0.02」的整数索引，虽然等比例放大了 50 倍（距离关系不变），但逐场景平移量不同、且丢失了米制直觉；更关键的是 `collate()` 的坐标在训练时可能被弹性扰动过，用它算质心会把增强噪声泄漏进「位置先验」。直接用原始点坐标最简单也最稳妥。

**练习 2**：`sp_centroids` 的行数由什么决定？如果某个超点编号在 `sp_pts_masks` 中不存在（空洞），质心矩阵会怎样？

**答案**：行数 = `sp_pts_masks.max() + 1`。出现空洞时，`scatter_mean` 会为缺失编号生成全零行（分母计数为 0 时的行为）——对应 4.2.4 末尾提到的现象。这也是 u3-l1 的偏移机制必须让全局超点编号**连续无空洞**的又一个原因：否则 `point_positions[i]` 与该场景超点特征 `point_feats[i]` 的行数对不上，触发 L1361 的防御分支。

**练习 3**：假设把 `max_point_tokens` 从 2000 调到 4000，哪些地方会受影响？

**答案**：直接受影响的是两个 FPS 聚合器的 `out_tokens`（query_decoder.py L954-L955，越少触发聚合、越多超点直接进 LMM）；间接影响是语言序列变长——注意力与 KV 显存约按 token 数平方/线性增长，训练显存占用上升、吞吐下降；但 3D 侧（collate、UNet、scatter_mean 池化）完全不受影响，因为压缩发生在「池化之后、进 LMM 之前」。这个参数是 3D 侧与语言侧之间的预算旋钮。

torch.manual_seed(0)
voxel_size, min_spatial_shape = 0.02, 128

# ---- 构造两个场景：场景 0 有 5 点 2 超点，场景 1 有 4 点 2 超点 ----
N0, N1, M0, M1 = 5, 4, 2, 2
points = [torch.rand(N0, 6), torch.rand(N1, 6)]            # (N,6): XYZ+RGB
sp_local = [torch.tensor([0, 0, 1, 1, 0]),                 # 场景 0 的逐点超点编号
            torch.tensor([0, 1, 1, 1])]                    # 场景 1 的逐点超点编号
elastic = [torch.rand(N0, 3) * 50, torch.rand(N1, 3) * 50] # 假装是 ElasticTransfrom 的产物(体素单位)

# ---- u3-l1 的偏移机制：全局化超点编号 + batch_offsets ----
batch_offsets, sp_all, bias = [0], [], 0
for sp in sp_local:
    sp_all.append(sp + bias)
    bias = (sp + bias).max().item() + 1
    batch_offsets.append(bias)
sp_pts_masks = torch.hstack(sp_all)                        # (N_total,)
M_total = bias
print(f'batch_offsets={batch_offsets}, M_total={M_total}')

# ---- 模块 4.1：collate（弹性分支 + 非弹性特征），手工版 ----
coords = torch.cat([torch.cat([torch.full((c.shape[0],1), float(b)), c - c.min(0)[0]], 1)
                    for b, c in enumerate(elastic)]).int() # (N_total,4)
feats = torch.cat([torch.hstack((p[:,3:], p[:,:3] - p[:,:3].mean(0))) for p in points])
uniq, inverse_mapping = torch.unique(coords, dim=0, return_inverse=True, sorted=True)
spatial_shape = torch.clip(uniq[:,1:].max(0)[0] + 1, min_spatial_shape)
print(f'量化: N_total={coords.shape[0]} → V={uniq.shape[0]}, '
      f'inverse_mapping={inverse_mapping.tolist()}, spatial_shape={spatial_shape.tolist()}')

# ---- 模块 4.2：extract_feat（UNet 用恒等映射代替，维度当作 6）----
voxel_feats = feats[torch.unique(inverse_mapping)]         # (V,6) “体素特征”
x = scatter_mean(voxel_feats[inverse_mapping], sp_pts_masks, dim=0)   # (M_total,6)
out = [x[batch_offsets[i]: batch_offsets[i+1]] for i in range(len(batch_offsets)-1)]
print(f'超点池化: (V,6)→(M_total,6)={tuple(x.shape)}, 切分后 '
      f'{[tuple(o.shape) for o in out]}')

# ---- 模块 4.3：point_positions 质心 ----
raw_pos = torch.vstack([p[:, :3] for p in points])
sp_centroids = scatter_mean(raw_pos, sp_pts_masks, dim=0)
point_positions = [sp_centroids[batch_offsets[i]: batch_offsets[i+1]]
                   for i in range(len(batch_offsets)-1)]
print(f'质心: (N_total,3)→(M_total,3)={tuple(sp_centroids.shape)}')

# ---- 手工核对：场景 0 超点 0 = 点 0,1,4 的特征均值 ----
ids0 = (sp_local[0] == 0).nonzero().squeeze(1)
manual = feats[:N0][ids0].mean(0)
assert torch.allclose(out[0][0], manual, atol=1e-5), '超点特征手算不一致!'
assert torch.allclose(point_positions[0][0], points[0][ids0][:, :3].mean(0), atol=1e-6)
print('场景0超点0 的特征与质心 手工核对通过')
```

**预期结果**（形状部分是确定的，数值部分待本地验证）：

| 检查点 | 预期形状 |
|---|---|
| `coords` | \((9, 4)\) |
| `inverse_mapping` | \((9,)\)，V ≤ 9 |
| `spatial_shape` | \([128, 128, 128]\) |
| 池化输出 `x` | \((4, 6)\)，即 \(M_{total}=4\) |
| 切分 `out` | \([(2,6), (2,6)]\) |
| `sp_centroids` / `point_positions` | \((4,3)\) / \([(2,3),(2,3)]\) |

两条断言通过即说明：超点特征确实是「组内点特征的平均」、质心确实是「组内点坐标的平均」。完成后，建议再回到真实源码对照：把 `voxel_feats` 那一行换成真的 `input_conv + unet + output_layer`（需要装好 u1-l2 的完整环境），其余代码不用改——这正是 `extract_feat` 的结构。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `collate()` 完成三件事：逐场景构造「体素坐标 + 6 维特征（RGB + 中心化 XYZ）」、用 `ME.utils.batch_sparse_collate` 拼 batch（第 0 列样本编号）、用 `ME.TensorField.sparse()` 去重得到 \((V,4)\) 坐标并返回 `inverse_mapping` 记录「每个点 → 所在体素」的回溯关系。
- 训练专用的 `elastic_coords` 只替换量化坐标（且在 `ElasticTransfrom` 中已除过体素长，`collate` 只做平移），点特征与全部逐点标签保持原始对齐——增强只改变「分组方式」，不改变「点的内容」。
- 超点池化一行 `scatter_mean(x.features[inverse_mapping], superpoints, dim=0)` 先把体素特征广播回点级、再按全局超点编号分组求均值，形状链为 \((V,32) → (N_{total},32) → (M_{total},32)\)，最后按 `batch_offsets` 切回逐场景。
- `point_positions` 用同一个 `scatter_mean` 对**原始米制坐标**求逐超点质心，仅当训练且超点数超过 `max_point_tokens=2000` 时被 `FPSPositionAggregator` 消费（按几何距离做 FPS 降采样）；推理路径计算但不使用。
- 点 → 体素的合并是 ME 量化的隐式行为（`inverse_mapping` 记录），体素/点 → 超点的平均是显式可导的 `scatter_mean`；评估时 `mask[:, superpoints]` 用同一份编号反向升采样，一降一升构成闭环。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

本讲之后，3D 侧（单元 3）就完整了：数据管线（单元 2）→ 主入口与 batch_offsets（u3-l1）→ 稀疏主干（u3-l2）→ 超点池化（本讲）。下一讲进入单元 4 的 LMM 侧，推荐顺序：

1. **u4-l1（点云 token 注入）**：本讲的输出 `out`（逐场景 \((M_i,32)\) 超点特征）在那里被 `point2token` 投影并 masked_scatter 到 Qwen3-VL 的 `<|point|>` token 位置——本讲 4.3.3 提到的 `max_point_tokens` 预算正是在那一步兑现。
2. **u4-l2（解码器初始化与 LoRA）**：看 `FPSAggregator`/`FPSPositionAggregator` 的完整实现与 `point2token`/`query_proj` 的维度变换。
3. 带着本讲的问题去读：超点特征同时作为 LMM 的输入 token 与分割解码器的 K/V（u1-l1 的双路设计），在 u5-l1 的解码器前向里观察这两条路如何汇合。

如果想在真实数据上验证本讲内容，推荐在跑通 u1-l4 的推理后，在 `extract_feat` 的 L1022 前后各加一行 `print` 打印 `x.features.shape` 与池化后形状（只加日志、不改逻辑），对照本讲第 5 节的形状表。

Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.
